evidence.note: Title states a specific declarative claim ('A shared rooftop array could undercut what blocks C and D pay for daytime power'), one sentence, no full stop, no hook.
Finding title with a number ('About 40% of what flats ... spend on electricity falls in daylight hours'); reader notes explain cause and consequence plainly.
Resident quote is verbatim under a neutral label ('Resident, block D') with no editorialising; title is a count-based finding.
Closing line 'Heavy daytime users get the largest credit.' is plain mechanism, not an epigram; captions are short and concrete.
Title 'Roof leaks, falling tariffs and later upkeep are the pilot's main risks' is a list-style claim rather than a sharper finding; bullets are concrete and sourced.
Title 'The board is asked to approve the £86,400 pilot...' reads as a procedural ask more than a finding; minor lapse against the title rule.
Byline 'Energy working group, November 2026' follows the '<name>, <Month year>' form.

rationale: Across all seven slides the copy follows the profile: findings as titles, plain cause-to-consequence notes, a verbatim quote, and no aphorisms, antitheses or hooks. The only lapses are titles on s-6 and s-7 that read as a list and a procedural ask rather than sharp findings, which the presenter might tweak. That fits level 4.
